## 1. 2026 IRS S-Corporation (Form 2553) vs. Disregarded Single-Member LLC Statutory Constants (`#1 C4`)

| Statutory Parameter | 2026 Official Value | IRC / IRS Authority |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Social Security (OASDI) Wage Base Cap** | **$176,100.00** | 26 U.S.C. § 3121 / SSA 2026 Cap |
| **OASDI Tax Rate (Combined Employer + Employee)** | **12.40%** (Max **$21,836.40**) | 26 U.S.C. § 3101(a), § 3111(a), § 1401(a) |
| **Medicare Hospital Insurance Rate (Uncapped)** | **2.90%** (1.45% + 1.45%) | 26 U.S.C. § 3101(b), § 3111(b), § 1401(b) |
| **Additional Medicare Surtax** | **0.90%** over **$200,000** (Single) / **$250,000** (MFJ) | 26 U.S.C. § 3101(b)(2) |
| **Schedule SE Net Earnings Multiplier** | **92.35%** (`1.0 - 0.0765`) | 26 U.S.C. § 1402(a)(12) |
| **Qualified Business Income (QBI) Deduction** | **20.00%** of Qualified Pass-Through Income | 26 U.S.C. § 199A (Excluded on W-2 Wages) |
| **S-Corp Owner FUTA/SUTA + Payroll/1120-S Baseline** | **$420.00** FUTA/SUTA + **$1,500.00** Payroll/CPA | Form 940 / Form 1120-S Compliance |

### Key 2026 S-Corp Break-Even Findings (Cite Directly):
1. **California (`CA`) $45,000 Net Profit Guardrail**: At `$45,000` net profit in California, an S-Corp election produces **negative net savings (`-$1,969.58/yr`)** due to California's mandatory `$800.00` minimum Franchise Tax (`R&TC § 23802`), `1.5%` entity-level S-Corp net income tax, `$1,920` payroll/CPA overhead, and lost Section 199A QBI deductions on W-2 wages. Single-Member LLC remains optimal below `~$72,000` in California.
2. **Texas (`TX`) & Florida (`FL`) $150,000 Net Profit Benchmark**: At `$150,000` net profit with an IRS safe-harbor `$57,000` W-2 reasonable salary, an S-Corp saves **`+$8,024.53/yr`** in Texas (`$0` Franchise Tax under `$2.47M` revenue) and **`+$8,012.74/yr`** in Florida.
3. **Non-Pass-Through Entity Tax Jurisdictions (`DC`, `TN`, `NH`)**: The District of Columbia (`8.25%` entity tax), Tennessee (`6.5%` Franchise & Excise Tax), and New Hampshire (`7.5%` BPT) tax S-Corporations at the entity level, negating standard federal FICA arbitrage.

## 2. 2026 USITC HTS Import Duty, Section 301, IEEPA & CBP Fee Constants (`#3 C5`)

| CBP / USITC Fee or Tariff Layer | 2026 Statutory Rate / Formula | Legal Citation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Merchandise Processing Fee (MPF - Formal Entry)** | **0.3464%** of FOB Customs Value | 19 CFR § 24.23(b)(1)(i)(A) |
| **CBP MPF Statutory Minimum Floor** | **$31.67** (Applies below `$9,142.61` FOB) | CBP FY2026 Federal Register Notice |
| **CBP MPF Statutory Maximum Cap** | **$614.35** (Reached at **`$177,352.77`** FOB) | CBP FY2026 Federal Register Notice |
| **Harbor Maintenance Fee (HMF - Ocean Only)** | **0.125%** of FOB Value (`$0.00` on Air/Truck) | 19 CFR § 24.24 / 26 U.S.C. § 4461 |
| **China Section 301 Tariffs (Chapter 99)** | **7.5% to 50.0%** (`9903.88.01` - `9903.91.03`) | 19 U.S.C. § 2411 (USTR 2025/2026 Action) |
| **China IEEPA Reciprocal / Emergency Tariff** | **20.0%** stacked ad valorem on FOB | 50 U.S.C. § 1701 et seq. (IEEPA) |

### High-Volume 2026 HTS Landed-Cost Benchmarks ($100,000 FOB Ocean Import from China):
- **`8507.60.0020` (Lithium-Ion EV & BESS Batteries)**: Base `3.4%` + Sec 301 `25.0%` (`9903.91.02`) + IEEPA `20.0%` + HMF `$125.00` + MPF `$346.40` = **`$48,871.40` Total Duties/Fees** (**`$152,571.40` Landed Cost** with `$3,700` CIF freight/ins). Reshoring to South Korea (`KR`) saves **`$48,400.00`**.
- **`8541.43.0010` (Solar PV Crystalline Modules)**: Base `0.0%` + Sec 301 `50.0%` (`9903.91.03`) + IEEPA `20.0%` + HMF `$125.00` + MPF `$346.40` = **`$70,471.40` Total Duties/Fees** (excluding `14.5%` AD/CVD risk).
- **`9403.20.0080` (Industrial Metal Warehouse Shelving)**: Base `0.0%` + Sec 301 `25.0%` (`9903.88.03`) + IEEPA `20.0%` + HMF `$125.00` + MPF `$346.40` = **`$45,471.40` Total Duties/Fees**. USMCA reshoring to Mexico (`MX`) saves **`$45,000.00`**.
